formats.key: approveAndCall(address spender, uint256 amount, bytes extraData)
effects: Sets the signer's tBTC allowance for `spender` to `amount` and replaces any earlier allowance.
If `amount` is type(uint256).max, the allowance is unlimited and `transferFrom` and `burnFrom` never reduce it.
Calls `spender.receiveApproval(signer, amount, tBTC, extraData)` in the same transaction, so the spender can take or burn up to `amount` tBTC from the signer at once.
When the spender is the tBTC Vault (as in case 0), it burns or takes the signer's tBTC and asks for a Bitcoin redemption to the output script inside `extraData`. That is the BTC the signer gets back.
Any allowance the spender does not use stays in place after the transaction.
formats.shown: The screen reads 'Approve and call tBTC', then shows the spender address, the amount (raw 1000000000000000000 in case 0) and the whole 'Redemption data' as raw hex.

findings.title: approveAndCall shows the redemption data as raw hex, so the BTC destination and redeemer are unreadable
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: {"path": "extraData", "label": "Redemption data", "format": "raw"}. Case 0 renders 'Redemption data' as 0x...79e21e5e...1111...aaaa...05f5e100...171600143bde42dcca7a1b985b7d2272ddce5b66d113feab.... ERC20WithPermit.approveAndCall passes extraData to IReceiveApproval(spender).receiveApproval.
findings.fix: Add a field that slices the redeemer address out of `extraData` (bytes 12 to 32) with format `addressName`. Add a field with the Bitcoin output script slice (from byte 224), labelled 'BTC output script'. Keep the full raw data at `visible: optional`.

findings.title: approveAndCall cannot show where the redeemed BTC goes as a Bitcoin address
findings.evidence: Case 0: extraData ends with the redeemerOutputScript 0x1600143bde42dcca7a1b985b7d2272ddce5b66d113feab (P2WPKH). ERC-7730 has no format that turns a Bitcoin script into a bech32 address.
findings.fix: Wait for a spec format for Bitcoin scripts. Until then, show the script slice with a clear label.

findings.title: approveAndCall intent 'Approve and call tBTC' does not say the spender takes or burns the tBTC now
findings.evidence: descriptor.json intent: "Approve and call tBTC". ERC20WithPermit.approveAndCall: `if (approve(spender, amount)) { IReceiveApproval(spender).receiveApproval(msg.sender, amount, address(this), extraData); }`. The tBTC token is the approved asset, not the contract that gets called.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Approve tBTC and call spender to use it", or "Redeem tBTC for BTC" if the descriptor is only meant for the tBTC Vault.

findings.title: approveAndCall labels extraData 'Redemption data' while the spender can be any contract
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: "label": "Redemption data" on `extraData`. The `spender` field accepts any contract address (types ["contract"]). ERC20WithPermit.approveAndCall forwards extraData to whatever `spender` is.
findings.fix: Change the label to 'Call data for spender', or describe it as redemption data only when the spender is the tBTC Vault.

findings.title: approveAndCall amount renders as the raw integer 1000000000000000000 with no tBTC unit
findings.evidence: Case 0 screen: {"label": "Amount", "value": "1000000000000000000"}. descriptor.json: "format": "tokenAmount", "params": {"tokenPath": "@.to"}. The descriptor has no metadata.token. The token is tBTC with 18 decimals.
findings.fix: Add "metadata": {"token": {"name": "tBTC v2", "ticker": "tBTC", "decimals": 18}}, or make sure `@.to` resolves to tBTC so the amount shows as 1 tBTC.

findings.title: approveAndCall shows a max-uint amount as a number, not as an unlimited allowance
findings.evidence: ERC20WithPermit.approveAndCall dev note: 'If the `amount` is set to `type(uint256).max` then `transferFrom` and `burnFrom` will not reduce an allowance.' The descriptor's `amount` field has no `threshold` or `message`.

couldNotCheck: approveAndCall calls the spender's receiveApproval. In case 0 that is the tBTC Vault 0x9C070027cdC9dc8F82416B2e5314E11DFb4FE3CD, then the tBTC Bridge. Neither source is in the directory, so I could not check from code how much tBTC leaves the signer, whether it is burned or moved, or how the redemption to the BTC output script runs.
